$comment: Node graph of everything in this repo worth retrieving. Startup does NOT load this -- it loads only the pointer to Get-Research.ps1, which queries it on demand. Progressive disclosure, DESIGN-NOTES section 2. Keep summaries one line: they are what retrieval matches against.
$comment.caveats: The 'caveats' array is what bites you: missing dependencies, external services contacted, platform assumptions, outright breakage. Shown on every retrieval, never hidden behind a flag. In ranking they DEMOTE and never select -- a term appearing in a node's problems is weaker evidence than the same term in its purpose, and a node should not surface merely for describing its own breakage. Add them via Add-ResearchNode.ps1 -Caveats.

nodes.summary: Manifest-driven startup: an explicit checkable contract of files to read and commands to run, instead of a prose context file that drifts silently.
Capability lives in per-topic skill files loaded on match, not one monolithic prompt; context is the scarce resource and instructions interfere.
Push/pop stack of investigation topics: debugging is depth-first search and working memory is not, so make the descent explicit and give it an unwind path.

Give the agent a compiler's semantic model rather than text search; query the narrowest slice first and read source only to spot-check. Rebuilt clean-room as RazorGraph.Mcp in D:\Repos\RazorGraphTool.
caveats: The implementation lives outside this repo (D:\Repos\RazorGraphTool, RazorGraph.Mcp) -- see note.razorgraph-mcp-server for shape and operational caveats. Extraction is Razor/ASP.NET-oriented; within this repo Get-LspReferences.ps1 still covers only reference lookup.

nodes.summary: Model emits a reviewable JSON plan of exact edit operations; a script executes it. Judgment from the model, mechanical execution from code.

Depersonalized review principles: capture why in comments, tests must be able to fail, move/rename PRs owe evidence, warning fixes must not change runtime defaults, runbooks never route to a named person.
Before an expensive query, force two questions: what am I trying to learn, and what is the cheapest query that distinguishes the hypotheses. Converts flailing into bisection.
Catch known-flaky tools inside the agent loop with explicit timeout and fallback; a hung call is indistinguishable from thinking, which is the worst failure mode.
Per-user/per-scope containers with scoped credentials rather than one shared store; centralized convenience is centralized failure and shared rate limits.

Handoff corpus format: one note per file, topic-prefixed filenames as the index, H1 plus one-sentence summary, cross-reference without deduplicating, machine-readable manifest as source of truth, density over polish, written for an LLM reader.

What to do differently: classify files portable/confidential/personal at authoring time, keep personal tooling in a personal repo from day one, never profile named colleagues durably, write operational discipline down early.

Executes startup-manifest.json: sets $env:JanetBase, validates every entry resolves before running anything, executes startup commands, emits a trimmed session brief (-Full for everything, -Text for the terminal).
caveats: Trims by default (-Full restores): strips $-prefixed manifest keys, reduces retrieval to graph/via/hint, emits rule text without why, omits run output already in captured. enforcedBy verification recognizes TWO wirings: project-level (Join-Path <project dir> <enforcedBy>) and user-level (~\.claude\settings.json names the script AND it exists at repo root) -- so ENFORCED labels survive foreign-dir sessions on this machine. An unwired hook NEVER fails startup: the rule is relabelled ADVISORY (claims ENFORCED; hook not wired here) and the note goes to the brief's own enforcement field plus the warning stream, NOT to problems (Start-Janet gates launch on problems). Only unresolved manifest entries are fatal, governed by onMissing. Runs from any working directory: everything resolves from $PSScriptRoot. Writes .janet\last-brief.json every run INCLUDING -Text; -OutFile moves it, an empty -OutFile skips writing. Adding a parameter renames every same-named local: $full/$text collided with -Full/-Text. See note.startup-brief-budget.

nodes.summary: Queries research.json by id, tag, kind, or scored free text, returning a ranked top-N shortlist; the single retrieval entry point so startup never loads the full inventory.
caveats: -Text is denser than the JSON for multi-node results (75% of the size: it drops the per-node field names), so it is the cheaper form for a model scanning a shortlist -- the opposite of Invoke-JanetStartup, where -Text is 251% because it adds every rule why. Choose by what the projection contains, not the flag name. -Text is written with Write-Host, so it cannot be captured by pipe, > redirection, or assignment; use 6>&1. See note.startup-brief-budget.

Indexing a large solution is slow and the script has no timeout, so a hung language server presents as a stalled session -- see pattern.circuit-breakers.

nodes.summary: Repo-agnostic pre-commit gate: PSScriptAnalyzer, deep nesting (christmas-tree, fail at >=6), Pester, config check, encoding audit. Staged files resolve against git rev-parse --show-toplevel from the CWD, so the one gate serves every repo (the Janet-level decision in note.pre-checkin-style-janet-level). Resolves git via JANET_GIT, then PATH, then the VS-bundled copy - no machine-specific hardcoding.
caveats: Test-Config.ps1 remains absent; that step self-skips.

$LASTEXITCODE is reset before each child-script step: a child that never calls exit leaves the previous child code in place, and the encoding step once failed on the nesting step verdict while printing All clean (caught by the 2026-08-03 smoke test).
C# nesting is not checked per-commit - no fast syntax-only path yet; the C# rule lives in RazorGraph deep_methods / query --deep at repo level.

Module requirements are conditional and fail legibly when unmet: PSScriptAnalyzer only when .ps1 files are staged, Pester 5+ only when *.Tests.ps1 files exist. Both installed CurrentUser 2026-08-03 (PSScriptAnalyzer 1.25.0, Pester 6.0.1); full gate verified green end-to-end on a clean staged file the same day.

nodes.summary: Lists all scripts with synopsis and parameter names by scanning the script directory; the exhaustive fallback when research.json lookup misses.
Lints .ps1 files against the mechanically checkable house rules: return @() unrolling, $null comparison order, truncating New-Item, plus 7-only syntax when -Target Ps51.

PowerShell rules for this repo, each written because it broke something: array unrolling on return, StrictMode property probing, $null comparison order, parameter/local name collisions, plus a 5.1 backward-compatibility section.
Personal research note on a hybrid insertion/merge sort; pure algorithms, tagged by its author as a shower thought that was not actually needed.
Expanded 56 KB version of the insertion/mergesort hybrid analysis.
Research note on .NET object sizing, covering public dotnet/runtime issue 24200 and observable public .NET behavior.
Notes on Meta's public AI Second Brain engineering blog post; third-party public material.

Original comparative analysis of Meta's Second Brain against Janet's architecture; sanitized of colleague names and internal system references. Updated 2026-07-31: Meta's newest post (DEmate, June 2026) independently converges on the tool-engine discipline - recipes, context injection, deterministic generation, explicit verification - but on the data-engineering side, while Second Brain itself still publishes no verification or staleness story. The note's update section argues this is a property of action-vs-recall, and of process-vs-artifact, not of talent.
The startup contract: files to read, commands to run, operating rules as { text, why }, and onMissing behavior. Executed by Invoke-JanetStartup.ps1.
caveats: Rules are { text, why, enforcedBy } objects; text is emitted every session, why only under -Full/-Text. Keep text to one line and put the argument in why. enforcedBy names the hook script backing an ENFORCED rule and is verified against the current project dir -- an unwired hook does NOT fail startup: the rule is relabelled ADVISORY and the mismatch is reported under the brief's enforcement field (not problems, which Start-Janet treats as fatal). Plain strings still parse. $-prefixed keys never reach the brief.

The user-level wiring lints every .ps1 written in ANY session on this machine against the JanetHome house rules -- deliberate, they are personal rules, but remember it when a lint message appears in an unrelated repo.

nodes.summary: App Service 500.30 with FileNotFoundException for a shared-framework assembly at startup: the ASP.NET Core Logging site extension version outran the worker runtime and its DOTNET_ADDITIONAL_DEPS injection broke resolution. Incident writeup with diagnosis path and fix.
caveats: VS publish can silently reinstall the extension at latest even with InstallAspNetCoreSiteExtension=false in the pubxml; Kudu PUT will not downgrade an installed extension in place - uninstall first. Recheck after every VS publish.
Slot swap moves the site extension with the content: after swapping, staging inherits the old production extension version (e.g. 9.0.4) - realign it before the next staging deploy.

Direction matters (confirmed 2026-07-28): extension NEWER than the installed runtime = startup death; extension OLDER than the runtime is ignored and harmless (a net10 app started clean alongside the 9.0.4 extension). Only realign when the extension version outruns the worker runtime.

nodes.summary: Manifest-driven build-and-deploy orchestrator: the generic pipeline (validate-first, git identity stamp, build/package/push gates, stamp-after-push, health poll distinguishing warming from broken, promote hint) lives here; each project declares only nouns in a deploy-manifest.json. Deploy sibling of the manifest-startup pattern.
caveats: Manifest command lines execute as trusted code in the repo root - the manifest is project config, not untrusted input. Only push type azureWebAppZip exists so far; add types in the switch when a new target platform appears. Verify counts only HTTP 200 as healthy. Get-Prop uses the Properties indexer deliberately: .Properties.Name -contains throws under StrictMode when the JSON object is empty.

nodes.summary: MCP stdio server over the RazorGraphTool code graph (D:\Repos\RazorGraphTool\src\RazorGraph.Mcp) - the DESIGN-NOTES section-4 graph-first pattern rebuilt clean-room; 21 tools, Janet JSON envelope conventions. Holds many graphs at once (keyed registry, optional graphId on every tool). build_solution spans a whole solution so Calls/InjectedInto cross project boundaries, and emits Covers edges from test methods to the code they exercise (full call closure, depth carried on each edge). Method-level detail: explicit constructors are Method nodes, using/await-using disposal is a Calls edge, bodyDepth nesting metric feeds deep_methods (the christmas-tree report), method_body_graph exposes one method's CFG with guard depths, method_body_diff proves two bodies flow-equivalent by bisimulation. Traversal takes a direction (outgoing/incoming/both) and descends containment for free. Extraction covers Razor/Roslyn topology, Class/Method nodes, wwwroot assets, and inline <script> blocks (2026-08-03).
caveats: build_graph and build_solution are slow (full Roslyn compile); build_solution compiles every project in the solution. Solution graphs scope Razor and client-asset ids by project name (page:<Project>/<relPath>, js:<Project>/<relPath>), so ids differ from single-project graphs of the same code.

.mcp.json launches a PUBLISHED copy -- D:/Repos/RazorGraphTool/.mcp-bin/RazorGraph.Mcp.exe, absolute path, gitignored -- refreshed with: dotnet publish src\RazorGraph.Mcp -c Release -o .mcp-bin. It used to launch the live bin/Debug output, which a running server locks, so any rebuild of that configuration failed with MSB3021 while a Claude session was up. Verified 2026-08-01 that Debug and Release solution builds both succeed with the server live. Residual: .mcp-bin itself is locked while a session runs, so re-publishing needs those sessions closed, and code changes reach the MCP tools only after re-publish AND a session restart.

Covers edges are call-graph reachability to the FULL call closure (since 73ddf10, 2026-08-02; was depth 3), not runtime coverage - a covered method is one some test can reach, not one a test asserted on. Each edge carries the depth it was reached at; filter on depth for direct exercise. Traversal seeds from the test and from its class lifecycle hooks and constructor. uncovered_methods excludes bodiless interface/abstract declarations, which never carry Covers edges.

Roslyn injection heuristic misclassifies positional-record constructor parameters as injectedServices (ConversionQueueStatus in ImageSelectorV2 lists int/long/List<string> as "services"). Needs a record/primitive exclusion. Still present as of 2026-08-03; the planned attribute-driven DI detection would fix it as a side effect.

No type-usage edges (return types, parameter types, property types): a DTO returned by a controller has zero edges even in a solution graph, so "who uses this type" is unanswerable for non-service classes - grep finds 6 files, the graph finds 0. Found 2026-08-01 querying ImageSelectorV2 saved graphs.

Saved-graph JSON field names differ from the in-memory model: edges serialize as from/to (not fromId/toId), node ids carry kind prefixes (type:, svc:, ctrl:, m:, page:, js:). Hand-written blob queries against the wrong names return empty and look like "no edges" - verify against the orientation view (Search-Json.ps1) first.

The published .mcp-bin predates exception_escapes (added 2026-08-07) until re-published; publish fails while any session holds the server open - close sessions first, then dotnet publish src/RazorGraph.Mcp -c Release -o .mcp-bin. The CLI twin (query --escapes) works immediately.

nodes.summary: The /deploy Claude Code skill: a thin trigger that routes any session (any project) to Invoke-BuildDeploy.ps1 and teaches it to query this graph instead of storing knowledge itself. Canonical file lives here; ~\.claude\skills\deploy is a junction to it.
caveats: The harness enumerates skill names and trigger descriptions ONCE at session start - a new or renamed skill is invisible until the next session, though content edits take effect on next invoke. Keep the file a pointer: invariants and graph queries only; new deployment lessons go in the graph, never in the skill. If the junction at ~\.claude\skills\deploy is ever deleted, recreate it with New-Item -ItemType Junction.

nodes.summary: OneDeploy reports Deployment successful while deploying nothing: a fossil WEBSITE_NODE_DEFAULT_VERSION=6.9.1 crashes Kudu deployment-script generation, OneDeploy swallows it, classic zipdeploy fails loudly. Every deploy for 4.5 months was a silent no-op. Verify content (file mtimes, route probes), never deployment status.
caveats: The tell is an impossibly fast successful deployment (~1s for 100MB) plus wwwroot mtimes older than the deploy. Health checks prove AN app runs, not WHICH app - probe a new-build-only route or file. SitePackages/packagename.txt residue is inert without WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE but muddies diagnosis.

nodes.summary: Scoping measurements for JS graphing in RazorGraph (2026-07-31): client tier is inline-first (575 <script> blocks / 14.5k LOC vs 24 js files / 3.7k in nopCommerce), DOM selectors dominate (2,362 sites vs 5 data-* uses), the literal-URL API rule scores 0% on real code where @Url.Action supplies the URL, and the vendor filter admits 102k LOC of lib_npm as first-party. Revised order: vendor fix, selector contracts, @Url.Action edges, function nodes; ESM/TS deferred.
caveats: Counts are regex over raw text - comments and string literals included, indicative not exact. Corpus = one personal app (ImageSelector, two versions of the same source) + nopCommerce (classic pole) + OrchardCore (bundled/TS pole). Selector-first and the @Url.Action finding hold at both poles; ESM/TS deferral survives but weakened - OrchardCore keeps sources outside wwwroot in Assets\, so graph-sources-vs-graph-shipped is an open design question for bundled projects.

nodes.summary: Generic JSON-blob search with Get-Research conventions: orientation view (arrays + field census), scored -Query, prop=value -Where filters with wildcards and dotted paths, -Select projection, { returned, totalMatches, truncated, items } envelope, -Text opt-in. Built 2026-08-01 for querying saved RazorGraph graphs without the MCP server; works on any JSON file whose interesting content is an array of objects.
caveats: Loads the whole file into memory (fine for MB-scale graphs). Unlike Get-Research it caps -Where results too (default -First 10) because blob arrays can hold tens of thousands of items; -All lifts the cap and the envelope always says when it was applied.

nodes.summary: Raw pieces for a personal essay: derive-dont-memorize as a lifelong strategy - quotient rule (~1983), associative memory vs names (the Naked story, IMDb as symbol table), Bresenham scaling and histogram statistics (1994), the three-queue dispatcher (2026), turns-into-scripts as Janet's origin, the essay-drafting method itself, and the late ADHD recognition that named the pattern. LT/J markers separate Lori's material from Claude's framings for the diff-against-perception editing pass.
caveats: Personal content (health, named-by-initial people, a friend's diary). Raw material, not a draft - the [J] framings are unvetted and must be diffed against perception before any public use. Published as a private artifact 2026-08-01; open questions at the bottom list facts to verify before drafting.

nodes.summary: The startup brief grew until 84% of it was non-contract prose; measurement, the trim, and the switch-parameter/local variable collision that adding -Full exposed.
caveats: The 54% reduction is measured against the 2026-08-01 manifest; re-measure after adding rules or retrieval fields. Trimming is done by the emitter, so growing manifest prose no longer costs the session but still costs -Full and -Text readers.

nodes.summary: Agent instructions for this repo: run Invoke-JanetStartup.ps1 yourself rather than accepting a pasted brief, and launch with JanetHome as the project dir so the hooks load.
caveats: Only loads when the session project dir is JanetHome -- which is the same condition the enforcement check tests. A session started elsewhere sees neither this file nor the hooks.

nodes.summary: Launcher: runs Invoke-JanetStartup.ps1, refuses to launch on any problems entry, then starts an interactive claude session with the brief as the opening prompt. -Path for the working dir (default cwd -- designed for loading Janet while working in another repo), -DryRun to preview, prompts over 24k chars staged through a temp file.
caveats: Gates launch on the brief's problems field, so anything added to problems becomes a launch blocker by contract -- enforcement notes went there briefly on 2026-08-01 and broke launching from any non-JanetHome directory, the launcher's primary case. Unwired-hook notes now arrive in the separate enforcement field, printed as yellow warnings without blocking. Windows caps a command line at 32767 chars with silent truncation, hence the 24k inline-prompt ceiling.

The prompt is ALWAYS staged through a file; only a quote-free pointer goes on the command line. Passing the brief inline shredded under Windows PowerShell 5.1 native-argument passing (embedded JSON quotes are not escaped), and claude read brief fragments as options: error unknown option -Query, 2026-08-01.

nodes.summary: Decision 2026-08-02: pre-checkin style fixing is a Janet-level, language-plugged gate for all code in every repo; Test-PreCommit.ps1 is the broken natural host.

Circuit-breaker wrapper for external commands (DESIGN-NOTES section 8 as code): captured StdOut/StdErr as line arrays, explicit timeout with kill, throws on failure by default; -NoThrow/-Quiet for caller-owned outcomes, -WorkingDirectory defaults to the caller's PowerShell location.

The move table for flattening deep nesting (christmas-tree code): guard inversion (universally legal, prover-blessable via method_body_diff), extract-method (only real fix for loop pyramids; prover correctly refuses, gate with tests + graph edge-set diff), compute-and-return (ctor fallback). Extract-method is compiler-forbidden in ctors assigning readonly fields (CS0191) or init-only properties (CS8852) - an auto-flattener must check MethodKind.Constructor plus what the block assigns. Includes the worked workflow from the prover's first production run (RazorGraphTool bc6693f, 2026-08-03).

The operating skill for the RazorGraph cluster: WHEN to reach for the graph (questions text search cannot answer - callers, implementers, blast radius, test reach, nesting, flow equivalence) and the workflow (build once/save/load, orient then drill, direction semantics, exact m:Type.Name(params) ids, coverage=reachability, body tools for method-level, mechanical refactor gates, source only to spot-check). Judgment here; depth delegated to the linked nodes; blind spots on note.razorgraph-mcp-server.

Split conditional tangles that are really dispatch: a discriminator front end that only routes, over a catalog of well-known fixed back ends (state machines as declarative queries) that only compute. Duplication corollary: copies behind a discriminator are enumerable inventory, not silently-drifting contraband - deliberately anti-DRY-reflex. RazorGraph-era tooling upgrades it: method_body_diff proves which back ends are merge candidates, coverage prices refactor risk upfront, and conformance (every path lands in exactly one back end, nothing routes around the front end) is a graph query. The tell: a method whose nesting grows every time the business adds a case.

Deep-nesting (christmas-tree) detector for PowerShell by AST - the PS backend of the style gate nesting rule, sibling of RazorGraph deep_methods. Reports functions and top-level script bodies nesting >= MinDepth, deepest first; elseif adds no depth (free from IfStatementAst.Clauses); script-block literals count one level because they indent. JSON envelope, -Text opt-in, exit 1 on findings so it gates directly. Calibration 2026-08-03 over JanetHome scripts: >=3 flags 35 containers, >=6 flags 3; gate threshold set to 6 from that data plus the RazorGraphTool precedent (5 is case-by-case).
caveats: Parse errors are reported and exit 1, never silently skipped - an unparseable staged file fails the gate by design. Counting script-block literals is a deliberate divergence from the C# metric (lambdas add no depth there): pipeline-style trees would otherwise vanish from the report.

nodes.summary: 2026-08-07 survey of the MCP code-graph field. Unique to RazorGraphTool: the flow-equivalence prover as refactoring gate, and Razor/PageModel/JS cross-boundary correlation. Near-unique: coverage-as-reachability (one other implementer: roslyn-codelens-mcp, the closest competitor - watch it). Commodity: call graphs/references/impact. Field is ahead on language breadth, incremental indexing, vector search, token economy, composable queries. Strategy: invest in prover + Razor to stay distinct; incremental indexing + Lua to catch up.

Concepts to borrow from the MCP code-graph field, tiered by fusion with unique assets. Tier 1: diff-aware test impact (Covers edges backward from git diff), MinHash similarity shortlisting for the prover (makes the section-12 pairwise sweep tractable), measured-coverage import (closes reachable-vs-asserted caveat), graph_diff tool, content-hash incremental indexing + syntax-only fast tier (solves fast per-commit C# nesting). Tier 3 synthesis: plan -> SurgicalEdit -> prover-verify closed loop. Not borrowed: cloud, language breadth, vectors.

Diagnose no-trace app exits as a reachability question: check the process exception surface first (one get_node), run exception_escapes for the throw-to-entry-point shortlist, rule reachable sites out, hunt catch-shape mismatches and non-total render-loop callbacks, then fix in four layers (site guard, operation catch, process backstop, crash log). Distilled from the RetirementCore.App first-run crash, 2026-08-07.
caveats: Delegate following added 2026-08-07 (RazorGraphTool a9c1c01): the pre-fix RetirementCore crash commit reports 44 escapes including both hand-found crashes (CheckedCents into the labeler callback; MonteCarlo.Run ArgumentException into RunAsync). The first increment reported zero on the same commit because every hop was delegate-mediated - kept here as the war story.
Remaining blind spots: stored-and-forwarded delegates (one hop only), local functions, virtual dispatch, BCL throwers, top-level-statement Main. Zero still means "no static chain", never "safe".

Escapes are prove-me-safe prompts, not confirmed bugs: value guards are invisible (a labeler that checks IsFinite before FromDouble still reports), and a process-level backstop like DispatcherUnhandledException is not a catch on any chain - an escape may surface as a dialog, not an exit.
